newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel-solution in sight in dispute with Buba.
newsitem.headline: Waigel-solution in sight in dispute with Buba.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Saturday that an amicable solution was on the horizon in the government's dispute with the Bundesbank over plans to revalue reserves.

"We have a solution in sight which we will achieve in agreement with the Bundesbank," Waigel said at a meeting of the Christian Social Union (CSU), sister party to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU).

Separately, CSU sources said that discussions over revaluing gold reserves were still continuing. Currency reserves would be revalued this year and the resultant profit reflected in state accounts for 1998, the sources said.

Bonn has been forced to back off a plan to receive a profit transfer from revaluing gold and currency reserves this year, the crucial year for selecting countries eligible for the planned 1999 euro launch.

The Bundesbank shot down the plan, arguing that it interfered with its independence and hurt Germany's reputation as a by-the-rules player on monetary union, but has declared itself willing to accept a modified revaluation scheme.
The precise terms of the new proposals under discussion are not clear, but the Bundesbank said after its council meeting on Thursday that it hoped a compromise would be reached soon.
Waigel stressed again that the dispute between Bonn and the fiercely independent central bank had been only over the timing of the revaluation process.
"Any fight between politicians and the Bundesbank does us no good," Waigel said.
